title: Fire escape
thoughtProcess: I was walking through Lower Haight in the early evening when the light hitting the side of this building reminded me of my childhood bedroom: a green wall brightened and warmed by the sunset.
I also found the composition enticing: the light against the cooler shadow, with laundry hanging out of the window. It reminded me of the beauty of the mundane, and I wanted to capture that.

title: Flower studies
thoughtProcess: I was walking through the Conservatory of Flowers, and these were some of my favorite plants in the museum. The one on the right is beautiful and has a whole ecosystem living in its center, with water, bugs, and bacteria.
I started with the flower in the middle, then expanded to the other two and thought they would work well as a triptych.
These flower studies were also a way for me to get more comfortable with gouache.

title: Portrait study
thoughtProcess: I’ve done self-portraits for most of my sketches throughout my life, whether I wanted to or not. I guess since I’m most familiar with my own face, I see nearly every face I draw as a reinterpretation of myself.
This was a quick study I did for an oil painting class before we started painting faces. I think I did a good job of capturing my likeness and getting the proportions right.

title: Sketchbook jam
thoughtProcess: This is a study of a character who is generally quiet in her everyday life. I think I was partially inspired by Gru from Despicable Me, but also by myself in middle school.
I was very shy because I was worried about what others thought of me, until music came on. Then I became a different person and felt like I could dance forever.
I’ve always loved to dance, and I think this is a good representation of how I feel when I get to express myself through dance.

title: The faces of Brooklyn
thoughtProcess: I drew this as an observation of the people I noticed walking around Brooklyn. I loved wandering around and had a 10-mile loop through Prospect Park, down to Green-Wood Cemetery, then back through Park Slope that I walked often. These are some of the people I saw along the way.

title: Character studies
thoughtProcess: This was an extension of a previous character study of a girl for my Illustration as Design class at SVA. I liked imagining her in different scenes and thought the umbrella being flipped inside out was funny.

title: Van Gogh Inspired Hands
thoughtProcess: This was an assignment for a studio class I took at UMD. The assignment was to draw five hands holding objects.

I had recently seen Van Gogh’s Irises and thought it would be interesting to make the hands themselves objects in a still life. I had them mimic the shapes flowers would take, holding leaves in similar ways.
This is one of the works I am most proud of.

title: Fishy Illustration
thoughtProcess: I love drawing fish because they’re so colorful and generally have interesting shapes. There’s also a fluidity to how they move through water that makes them fun to draw. With this piece, the idea was to capture some of that movement and variety in a fun interpretation of fish.

I was trying to move more into an illustration mindset, using flatter elements like the bubbles and lines to show the undercurrents you would see under the sea. This was also an exercise in drawing fish from many different perspectives and figuring out how to show their shapes from different angles.

title: Pixel plants
thoughtProcess: These two drawings were for a friend’s side project in college. When Dynamic Island came to the iPhone, my friends wanted to create an app with a little digital plant that would live on your phone. You could water it every day and watch it grow.
I thought it would be cool to learn how to make those kinds of designs, so I created these two for the project.

title: Kestrel
thoughtProcess: This was a commission from my friend’s startup in college, which was a bank specializing in providing loans to agriculture. Since the name of their startup was Kestrel and it previously had a bird design on it, I took the same bird design but made it more explicit in its messaging of providing support to agriculture.
The lines represent the lines of crops you would see in the field, but can also be interpreted as the wing of the kestrel.

title: A Japanese tea garden tree
thoughtProcess: I’ve always struggled more with digital art because I usually use the material to help inspire the drawings I like to do. As someone who is color-forward, having access to an unlimited color palette can lead to a less curated drawing.

This was the first drawing where it clicked for me to try a more illustrative approach. I wasn’t going to get the same textures as physical mediums with digital art, so I needed to create the texture myself through hatching and shading, and by creating interesting lines.
